title: Latency budget audit
summary: Pick one LLM feature, write its latency budget, then measure a real streaming endpoint against it: TTFT, inter-token latency and end-to-end time at P50, P90, P95 and P99 for two prompt shapes. The README opens with a verdict on whether the endpoint meets the budget.
deliverables: A streaming client that logs one JSON line per request to data/requests.jsonl: send time, first-token time, every token arrival time, end time, token counts and status.
At least 150 measured requests for each of two prompt shapes (a short input and a long input), after warm-up.
An analysis script that turns data/requests.jsonl into results.json.
A Makefile whose check target recomputes the percentiles from data/requests.jsonl and fails if they disagree with results.json.
A README that opens with the verdict and names the term that misses the budget, if any.
constraints: Time every event on the client with a monotonic clock, and stream the response.
Any endpoint works: a hosted API or a model on your own machine. Name the model and where it ran.
Leave warm-up requests out of the numbers and report how many you dropped.
Commit the raw request log. Keep API keys out of the repo.
make check uses the Python standard library only and needs no network.

criteria: The budget belongs to a named feature and a named kind of user (see 1.2).
TTFT, inter-token latency and end-to-end time get separate targets, each at a stated percentile.
The README says why each target has the value it has.
Every request has client-side timestamps for the first token and each later token.
Warm-up requests are excluded and counted.
Both prompt shapes have at least 150 measured requests, with input and output token counts recorded.
Someone else could rerun the client from the README alone.
Percentiles in results.json match the raw log (make check proves it).
The README compares mean with P50 and explains what drives the tail (see 1.4.1).
The README separates network and queue time from inference time where the data allows (see 1.4.2).
The verdict comes first and gives the margin in milliseconds.
Every number in the README appears in results.json.
Limitations name what this setup cannot tell you.

checks.label: Required files are in the repo
make check passes on CPU and prints "audit ok"
